caption: Grady v. North Carolina
node: searches/the-third-party-doctrine-and-digital-surveillance/Real-Time Tracking (also Two Definitions of Search — trespass/Jones line)
justification: Per curiam. Attaching a satellite-based ankle monitor to track a recidivist sex offender's movements IS a Fourth Amendment search under the Jones/Jardines trespass theory ('the State ... physically ... attach[ed] that device to a person's body, without consent, for the purpose of tracking that individual's movements'); remanded for reasonableness. Controlling SCOTUS extension of Jones to compulsory GPS monitoring in the civil/regulatory setting — corpus has Jones and Karo/Knotts but LACKS Grady (grep 0). Fills the Real-Time Tracking placed-empty node with a SCOTUS anchor and completes the trespass-tracking line on Two Definitions of Search.
gate: INGEST prong (a) field conduct / (b) admissibility — search-threshold ruling officers rely on for tracking devices
notes: Confirm cluster + per-curiam status at S2 R7 queue; not in GAP docket or A1/A2 sub-legs.

caption: People v. Seymour
justification: First state high court to rule on a REVERSE-KEYWORD (Google search-term) warrant. Held under the COLORADO Constitution (greater protection than 4A) that defendant had a protected privacy interest in his search history tied to IP, but upheld admission on good faith. State + state-constitution ground => persuasive/illustrative only; NOT binding, NOT a federal split. Populates the Reverse-Keyword stub as a lower-court-development bullet (S5 R11), not a page.
gate: INGEST-adjacent (admissibility) but below the D5 frontier floor
notes: Reverse-keyword search-threshold question has no SCOTUS and no federal circuit holding yet — frontier unsettled.

caption: Long Lake Township v. Maxon
justification: Drone-surveillance frontier. Michigan COA held low-altitude, targeted, warrantless drone surveillance of a home/curtilage is 'qualitatively different' from manned-aircraft overflight (Ciraolo/Riley) and encroaches on REP => a search; the Michigan Supreme Court declined to reach the 4A question and resolved on exclusionary-rule inapplicability. State only, no SCOTUS drone decision; the manned-aircraft lineage (Ciraolo/Riley/Dow) is the bridge but may not fit. Below the frontier floor (not binding-in-circuit, not a federal split) => mention on the Aerial & Enhanced Surveillance / drone frontier.
notes: Confirm final MSC disposition/cite at S2; corpus already treats drones as jurisdiction-dependent/unsettled on the Third-Party Doctrine page.

caption: State v. Andrews (Maryland v. Andrews)
justification: Leading state appellate decision holding use of a cell-site simulator (Stingray/Hailstorm) to locate a phone is a Fourth Amendment search requiring a warrant (real-time location, active signal-forcing device). State intermediate appellate; no SCOTUS and no binding federal circuit holding on cell-site simulators (grep: corpus has ZERO cell-site-simulator/Stingray cases). Populates the Cell-Site Simulators stub as a lower-court-development bullet, not a page.
